page.summary: Convert one Exhaustion trigger into distance or the next loop, then return to objective tempo when the route or activation window is gone.

verdict.recommendation: Choose the trigger that matches the route you can reach; do not treat five named options as one four-perk build.
verdict.soloQ: Use the burst to leave danger or reach the next usable resource, then repair or rescue when the Killer declines the chase.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call where you are taking chase and which route is being spent so teammates can keep the next objective clear.
verdict.mainWeakness: Exhaustion management and trigger conditions can leave the selected tool quiet; over-saving a burst can also cost more tempo than it returns.

plans.label: Mobility trigger choices
plans.why: Choose one mobility trigger; these are alternatives, not a simultaneous four-perk build.

choices.whyItsHere: Use a rushed vault to launch toward the next resource.
Start the escape toward a useful route when the trigger is available.
Use a safe fall to convert height into distance when the map offers it.
Reserve the post-unhook injured chase timing for the moment it actually applies.
Use the hit-created sprint to leave the first danger area when healthy-state conditions apply.
Recover Exhausted more efficiently when staying near the support effect is worth the time.

opening: Choose the trigger that fits the route before pressure starts; do not treat every listed choice as equipped.

rows.situation: A trigger is available and the next route has a real resource.
rows.action: Commit the trigger toward that resource, then reassess instead of looping for the perk alone.
rows.why: Mobility only buys team value when it creates a better next position.

rows.situation: The route or activation condition is denied.
rows.action: Stop forcing the trigger and return to the available objective, rescue or safest remaining route.
rows.why: A denied activation is an opportunity cost, not a reason to chase the original plan.

abortWhen: Stop preserving Exhaustion when walking or repositioning costs more than the next useful activation can repay.
Leave a depleted route when the next resource cannot support another loop.

soloQ: Do not assume a long chase means teammates are repairing; once the trigger has moved you, check which job is actually uncovered.
coordinatedSwf: Call the chase route and spent resource so teammates can keep repairs away from the depleted area and hand off when the Killer switches.

strengths: Reliable chase extension without total build commitment.
weaknesses: Exhaustion management and trigger conditions limit repeated value; Sprint Burst currently gives a shorter burst than before.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can change targets, route you away from the activation geometry or force resources out before committing to the chase.
commonMistakes: Walking or repositioning only to preserve a burst when ordinary objective work would repay more.
Forcing the trigger after its value window has passed instead of returning to repair or rescue tempo.
Adding same-purpose mobility until the module becomes dead slots when the Killer refuses the interaction.
